regions.label: paragraph_title
regions.text: THE OLD AND THE NEW

regions.label: text
regions.text: Blackwell's Island reveals two striking illustrations of the woman of the past and the woman of the future. Katherine B. Davis is the woman of the past and Rebecca Edelson is the woman of the future.

regions.label: text
regions.text: Katherine B. Davis was carefully trained in her youth for college; her college training helped and fortified her to become Police Matron of Bedford Reformatory for Women, and subsequently Commissioner of Corrections of New York. Both worthy offices to uphold the present system.

regions.label: text
regions.text: Katherine is a staunch defender of the present society, despite her experiences among "the fallen" and her knowledge that poverty and destitution has driven them to prostitution.

regions.label: text
regions.text: Becky on the other hand comes from that race of people whose spirit has refused to be enslaved.

regions.label: text
regions.text: Becky has never been to college but she knows more about existing conditions and their causes, about poverty, prostitution and their causes than Katherine learned in all her arderous years of college education. Becky considers such an calling as Police Matron as base and looks upon it with contemptous acorn.

regions.label: text
regions.text: Her ideals of womanhood are high. Her service to womankind is to free them. Katherine's position is to keep women in bondage. Becky's idea is to free all womankind.

regions.label: text
regions.text:
Katherine aims to keep women tame in submission to the chains of the present slavery.
Recky aims to inspire them with revolt against the chains and the system which has enslaved them.

regions.label: text
regions.text: THE WOMAN REBEL

regions.label: text
regions.text: In the background of these two women stands two greater forces which is a question of time when they too shall be in the death struggle similar to that taking place on Blackwell's Island, Capital on Miss Davis' side and Labor on Becky Edelson's side.

regions.label: paragraph_title
regions.text: MORE JUSTICE!

regions.label: text
regions.text: Imprisoned Comrades of the working class have been saved again and again from the clutches of the monster Capitalism, but from the turn the trials have taken in the Rangle-Cline case those of us on the outside will have to awaken to our consciousness and act without delay if those boys are to be saved.

regions.label: text
regions.text: Fourteen of our boys have been in jail in Texas for more than a year, several of them have been tried and have received the following sentences: J. Gonzales, 99 years; L. Vasques who had been sentenced to serve fifteen years, appealed his case and the decision was reversed by the Texas Court of Appeals, AND TEN MORE YEARS WERE ADDED TO HIS SENTENCE.

regions.label: text
regions.text: How is this for Justice for the workers? J. A. Serrato, 25 years; L. Gonzales, 6 years; and M. P. Martinez, 12 years. What Rangel, Cline and the other boys not yet tried will get one can almost predict, unless SOME- THING DEFINITE and SPECI- FIC is acted upon at once.

regions.label: text
regions.text: Get into communication at once with Victor Cravello, Room 108, Los Angeles, Cal., and save these boys.

regions.label: paragraph_title
regions.text: CONFISCATED

regions.label: text
regions.text: Once again I must annouce that another issue of the Woman Rebel has been debarred from transmission by the Post Office authorities, and all the copies found in the mails have been CONFISCATED.

regions.label: text
regions.text: That will account for the loss of your July number, if you did not get it.

regions.label: text
regions.text: It will be interesting to learn just what article in the July issue was considered OBSCENE. My suspicions are that it was one of two articles. One an excellent and scientific Defence of Assassination, by Herbert A. Thorp of which only one half was published in the July issue and the remaining part following later. The other was an editorial "Are Preventive Means Injurious" ! written in answer to the many questions I have received on this subject.

regions.label: text
regions.text: Both are questions which should be openly discussed, and through which enlightenment may be gained. The fares of Freedom of Speech is being forcibly recognized on Blackwell's Island where Becky Edelsohn is

regions.label: text
regions.text: resisting an unjust imprisonment for speaking the truth about the Mexican war. The farce of Freedom of Press is again being demonstrated by the three suppressions of the Woman Rebel within five months.

regions.label: paragraph_title
regions.text: WHERE IS YOUR POWER NOW ?

regions.label: text
regions.text: What is wrong with Germany's four or five million Socialists?

regions.label: text
regions.text: The answer is plain. Germany represents Autocracy and Imperialism. No matter how strong the Socialist movement may be in Germany, it has proved its shallowness and weakness in the present crisis. German Socialists ought to learn that Socialism under an Imperialistic Monarchy is a farce—a parody of the Revolutionary movement. Small wonder, then, that our feelings and sympathies must be with the French who have always labored champions of human liberty.

regions.label: paragraph_title
regions.text: THE WAR'S LESSON

regions.label: text
regions.text: If this European war does not convince the workers of the absolute necessity of SOLIDARITY, if this thrilling slaughter does not show working women that they must control the true destinies of a newer Civilization not based on Murder, then there is no reason for any revolutionary movement at all. We are hearing much cant and hypocrisy these days about peace and anti-militarism. The truth is that we do not want peace based on inevitable and certain Murder, on potential warfare. We are glad to witness the collapse of a hypocritical Civilization that can end only in wholesale Murder.

regions.label: text
regions.text: Exponents of birth-control have long pointed out why nations need men why rulers need them. Now every woman can see this in the savage slaughter of the children she brings into the world.

regions.label: text
regions.text: The war is good. No better education could be given the workers.

regions.label: text
regions.text: After the tumult and the murder ceases, workers will realize to what ends availed their slavish toil—what was the aim of this flamboyant civilization. Comrades killed, life made even more precarious, the burden of it all on the shoulders of working men and women.

regions.label: text
regions.text: The war is good. It is a challenge to the working class. It is a challenge we cannot avoid. It proves the murderous insanity of present day harbarism. Let us accept the challenge, and begin a new era at once.
